question: Can a small vision model trained only on ARC-derived data solve unseen ARC tasks by treating each grid transformation as task-conditioned image-to-image translation, and which spatial priors, synthetic training data, test-time parameter updates, and multi-view decoding account for its performance?

key_findings.claim: VARC makes ARC a task-conditioned per-pixel classification problem rather than explicitly inducing a symbolic program.
key_findings.evidence: For each task T, a learned task embedding conditions f_theta; the model minimizes per-pixel cross-entropy D(y_i, f_theta(x_i | T)). Inputs and outputs are discrete grids of at most 30 by 30 cells, but are embedded on a larger canvas and processed by a ViT or U-Net. The formulation learns the input-output mapping directly and contains no explicit rule language, search trace, or executable intermediate hypothesis.

anchors.section: 3.1 ARC Problem Definition and 3.2 Image-to-Image Translation, Equation 1

key_findings.claim: The distinctive representation combines a 64 by 64 canvas, 2 by 2 patchification, separable 2D position encoding, and integer scale and translation augmentation.
key_findings.evidence: A raw categorical grid is integer-rescaled by nearest-neighbor duplication, randomly translated while remaining visible, embedded with a separate background color, and divided into patches. Each discrete cell first receives a learned continuous embedding. The paper argues that a 2 by 2 patch can express many local color combinations and that scale and translation augmentation supply priors a vanilla ViT lacks.

anchors.section: 3.3 Visual Modeling, Translation and scale invariance, Vision Transformer, and 2D positional embedding

key_findings.claim: The system's inference procedure is computation-heavy adaptation and voting even though each final candidate is produced by a feedforward network.
key_findings.evidence: For every unseen task, VARC initializes a new task token and fine-tunes the whole task-specific model for 100 epochs on the 2 to 4 demonstrations augmented into 50 auxiliary flip/rotation/color-permutation tasks plus the original task. With three raw demonstrations this is 15,300 training samples. It then evaluates 510 random scale/translation views and retains the two most common exact output grids. The reported profile is about 0.7 seconds per test-time-training epoch, or roughly 70 seconds per task on one H100 before accounting for the stated multi-view forwards.

anchors.section: Tables 4-5 and Appendix A.2 Test-time Training Augmentation

key_findings.claim: The strongest single model reaches 54.5 percent pass@2 on ARC-1, while the ViT-plus-U-Net ensemble reaches 60.4 percent; only the single-model result reports run dispersion.
key_findings.evidence: Table 3 reports the 18M-parameter ViT at 54.5 plus or minus 0.7 over four runs and the 73M-parameter ensemble at 60.4. The ensemble combines an 18M ViT and 55M U-Net, each test-time-trained four times, but no ensemble uncertainty is given. Average human performance is listed as 60.2 and best-human performance as 98.0, so 'matching average human' is a narrow ARC-1 aggregate comparison rather than human-level parity across people or tasks.

key_findings.claim: ARC-2 is the central negative result: the single model falls to 8.3 percent and the ensemble to 11.1 percent despite the strong ARC-1 headline.
key_findings.evidence: Table 3 reports 8.3 plus or minus 0.4 for the single model and 11.1 for the ensemble on ARC-2, versus 54.5 and 60.4 on ARC-1. The ARC-2 models receive only ARC-1 offline training before ARC-2 test-time adaptation. For context, the same table lists best human at 100.0, TRM at 7.8, Grok-4-thinking at 16.0, and a Bespoke Grok-4 system at 29.4. VARC therefore improves the small-from-scratch comparison modestly but does not close the hard-distribution gap.

anchors.section: Figure 18, successful and failed ARC-2 examples

key_findings.claim: The visual-prior ablation is large but is a single cumulative intervention path rather than a factorial causal decomposition.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 7 rises from 26.8 for the naive baseline to 32.8 with 2D absolute positions, 43.0 with 2D RoPE, 45.4 after changing from 1 by 1 patches on 32 by 32 to 2 by 2 patches on 64 by 64, 48.3 with full translation augmentation, and 54.5 with scale augmentation. The authors summarize a 27.7-point total gain and 11.5 points for canvas-based changes. Because each row modifies the preceding system, patch size, canvas size, token cardinality, translation range, and positional treatment are partly bundled; the figure supplies no seed bars or reverse-order controls.

key_findings.claim: Scaling the ViT helps only up to the 18M configuration in the reported regime, and the 66M model is an explicit overfitting case.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 reports ViT accuracies of 44.4, 54.5, and 53.0 for 6M, 18M, and 66M parameters at 10, 28, and 99 Gflops. U-Net variants reach 42.8, 47.5, and 48.3 for 7M, 17M, and 55M parameters. The paper states that the 66M ViT has higher training accuracy but worse evaluation accuracy and directs future work toward generalization. These are architecture-size comparisons without matched FLOPs or uncertainty.

anchors.section: Table 1, Figure 8, and 5.2 Other Ablation Experiments

key_findings.claim: Independent per-task adaptation is about ten points better than joint adaptation, providing a negative result for sharing test-task updates.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 9 reports 54.5 with offline pretraining and independent test-time training versus 44.8 with offline pretraining and joint test-time training. Without offline training the respective results are 26.4 and 29.1. The paper hypothesizes that joint overtraining forgets offline knowledge, but gives no parameter-drift, retention, early-stopping, or matched-update analysis to test that mechanism.

key_findings.claim: A substantial part of the headline accuracy comes from 510-view decoding rather than a single prediction.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 reports 35.9 percent single-view pass@1, 49.8 multi-view pass@1, and 54.5 multi-view pass@2. Thus augmentation and exact-grid majority voting add 13.9 points at pass@1 and the second retained mode adds another 4.7 points. The system-level comparison does not normalize competitor inference calls, adaptation steps, or candidate budgets.

anchors.section: 3.5 Inference, Multi-view inference and Pass@2 accuracy
Table 2 and Single-view vs. multi-view inference

key_findings.claim: Performance depends strongly on synthetic examples and training-task diversity, so 'ARC-only' does not mean training only on the original few demonstrations.
key_findings.evidence: Offline training expands 400 ARC-1 tasks with 1,000 RE-ARC pairs per task, producing about 400,000 pairs. Appendix Figure 14 reports 31.5 without RE-ARC and 38.6, 52.3, and 54.0 with 10, 100, and 1,000 generated pairs per task. Figure 15 reports 26.4, 43.1, 49.6, and 54.5 when training on 0, 16, 80, and 400 tasks. RE-ARC generators encode hand-reconstructed transformation logic, making data-generation fidelity and generator overlap important confounds even though no internet-scale pretraining is used.

anchors.section: Figures 14-15 and Appendix B.1 Offline Training Data Scaling

key_findings.claim: The pass@k curve shows that the model sometimes contains a correct view without ranking it highly enough for pass@2.
key_findings.evidence: For the 18M ViT on ARC-1, pass@1, pass@2, and pass@300 are 49.8, 54.5, and 66.3 from the same 510 views. The paper calls 66.3 an oracle-like upper bound and notes that correct predictions are sometimes too sparsely populated to survive majority voting. This is useful failure evidence: candidate generation and candidate selection are separate bottlenecks.

anchors.section: Figure 16 and Appendix B.2 Pass@k Results

key_findings.claim: Output-shape handling adds task-specific machinery beyond a plain segmentation ViT, and its contribution is not isolated quantitatively.
key_findings.evidence: The canvas uses a background token and adds border tokens on the right and bottom of every output; inference crops at the rightmost and bottommost predicted borders. Attention masks suppress background keys, and training loss is computed only where inputs are not background. The appendix says these choices improve accuracy based on preliminary experiments but reports no ablation, including no rate of invalid or wrongly cropped shapes.

anchors.section: Appendix A.3 Shape Handling and Figure 13

key_findings.claim: The attention maps and task-embedding t-SNE are descriptive visualizations, not evidence that the model recovers human-interpretable rules.
key_findings.evidence: Selected attention maps appear local in early layers and more task-specific in later layers, and nearby t-SNE points receive similar human-written descriptions. No probe accuracy, intervention, attention-faithfulness test, neighborhood statistic, selection protocol, or random-seed replication is reported. One attention example marked with an asterisk is explicitly unsolved, showing that plausible maps need not imply a correct output.

key_findings.claim: The qualitative appendix documents both simple-looking failures and rule ambiguity that pass@2 cannot fully resolve.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 17 and 18 display solved and unsolved ARC-1/ARC-2 tasks; the authors explicitly state that some failures are simple for humans. Figure 19 shows demonstrations consistent with both a 'line passes through' and a 'line touches' rule, and VARC returns one of each as its two candidates. Figure 22 shows three selected tasks improving during adaptation, but supplies no denominator for how often trajectories converge, regress, or overfit.

key_findings.claim: The recurrent-model comparison establishes a reported-score advantage but does not isolate whether vision, synthetic data, adaptation compute, or candidate count causes it.
key_findings.evidence: Table 3 lists VARC at 54.5/8.3 on ARC-1/ARC-2, HRM at 40.3/5.0, and TRM at 44.6/7.8, all described as trained from scratch on ARC data. VARC nevertheless uses 400,000 RE-ARC pairs, 100 per-task update epochs, and 510 views; the table provides no matched data generator, GPU budget, number of attempts, test-time updates, or common replication. The result supports system-level superiority under each paper's recipe, not a controlled claim that feedforward vision is intrinsically better than recurrence.

method.core_idea: Represent categorical ARC grids as augmented images on a fixed canvas, train one small shared visual backbone across ARC-1 tasks, and adapt a fresh task embedding and model to each unseen task before decoding many transformed views.
method.mechanism: A categorical grid is integer-scaled and translated on a 64 by 64 canvas with explicit background and output-border tokens. A 2 by 2-patch ViT with separable 2D RoPE, or alternatively a U-Net, maps the canvas to per-pixel categorical logits under a task token and per-pixel cross-entropy. Offline training uses original ARC-1 demonstrations plus 1,000 RE-ARC generated pairs per training task. At test time, 2 to 4 demonstrations become 51 task variants through flips, rotations, and color permutations; the model trains for 100 epochs, predicts 510 scale/translation views, pools pixels back to the raw grid, and returns the two most frequent exact output grids. An ensemble repeats adaptation four times for each of an 18M ViT and 55M U-Net.
assumptions: The transformation governing an unseen ARC task can be recovered by gradient adaptation from 2 to 4 demonstrations after offline training on other tasks.
Integer scale and translation invariance are valid for the target rule, while rotations, reflections, and color permutations can be separated safely through distinct auxiliary task embeddings.
RE-ARC's procedurally generated examples faithfully expand each training task without injecting misleading generator-specific shortcuts.
A fixed 64 by 64 canvas contains every augmented grid and border token needed at train and test time.
Per-pixel cross-entropy and foreground-only loss are adequate surrogates for exact whole-grid pass@2 accuracy.
The rightmost and bottommost predicted border tokens reliably determine output shape.
A 2 by 2 patch representation preserves the cell-level distinctions needed for rules while helping rather than harming exact geometry.
The modal exact outputs across 510 random views are better candidates than lower-frequency but potentially correct outputs.
The public ARC-1 evaluation set and four adaptation runs adequately estimate generalization to hidden or harder ARC distributions.
System-level comparisons remain informative despite different pretraining data, synthetic generators, update counts, candidate budgets, and inference hardware.
Attention maps and proximity in a two-dimensional t-SNE projection reflect meaningful learned structure rather than visualization artifacts.
Average human ARC-1 accuracy is a relevant target even though participant skill, attempt budget, and ARC-2 performance differ.

techniques.role: Places variable-size ARC grids on a fixed background so standard image architectures can process random integer scales and translations.
Uses 2 by 2 categorical patches to expose local multi-color configurations instead of only ten single-cell tokens.
Encodes horizontal and vertical coordinates separately and supplies the ViT with explicit two-dimensional geometry.
Shares a visual backbone while giving each offline or auxiliary task its own learned embedding.
Updates the model for 100 epochs on demonstrations from one unseen task to infer its transformation.
Builds flip, rotation, and color-permutation auxiliary tasks while retaining scale and translation as within-task invariances.
Aggregates 510 augmented predictions by exact-output frequency and returns the two largest modes.
Predicts right and bottom border tokens to recover outputs whose dimensions differ from the input.
Masks background keys and excludes background-input locations from the loss to counter canvas class imbalance.
Combines independently adapted ViT and U-Net candidates to increase ARC pass@2.

limitations: Author-stated: the 66M ViT overfits despite higher training accuracy, so larger models require better generalization rather than simple scaling.
Author-stated: ARC-2 remains very difficult; single and ensemble results are only 8.3 and 11.1 percent.
Author-stated: test-time training each task independently is substantially better than joint adaptation, and the proposed explanation of forgetting is only a hypothesis.
Author-stated: some tasks simple for humans remain unsolved, and demonstrations can admit multiple plausible rules.
Author-stated: pass@300 exceeds pass@2 because correct views can be too rare for majority voting, so proposal selection remains a bottleneck.

Reviewer-identified: the strongest model is trained on roughly 400,000 ARC-derived pairs produced by hand-authored RE-ARC generators, so 'trained from scratch solely on ARC data' should not be read as original-data-only few-shot learning.
Reviewer-identified: most ablations are single cumulative curves or bars without seed-level uncertainty, hypothesis tests, or factorial controls.
Reviewer-identified: system comparisons do not match synthetic data, optimization steps, inference calls, pass budgets, hardware, or ensemble counts.
Reviewer-identified: the ensemble's 60.4 percent and most ablation cells have no run dispersion, while only the single model reports mean plus or minus standard deviation.
Reviewer-identified: output-border tokens, foreground-only loss, and background attention masks are unisolated implementation components, so a 'vanilla ViT' description is incomplete.
Reviewer-identified: no hidden ARC test-set result, task-level confidence interval, paired significance test, or error taxonomy estimates robustness beyond the public evaluation sets.
Reviewer-identified: qualitative attention and t-SNE plots do not establish faithful rule induction, abstraction, or causal reasoning.
Reviewer-identified: the claim that inference is feedforward excludes the 100-epoch parameter-adaptation loop and 510-view voting that precede each final answer.
Reviewer-identified: the fixed 64 by 64 canvas and integer-rescaling scheme impose a representational ceiling not tested on larger grids or transformations outside ARC's present limits.
failure_modes: A novel rule outside the transformations represented in offline ARC/RE-ARC tasks may not be recoverable from 2 to 4 examples by local gradient updates.
Synthetic RE-ARC shortcuts can encourage memorization of generator conventions rather than composition of the intended latent rule.
Independent test-time training can overfit demonstrations or forget reusable offline knowledge; joint adaptation already shows a roughly ten-point negative result with offline training.
A correct output may occur in only a few views and be discarded by exact-grid majority voting, as the pass@300 versus pass@2 gap demonstrates.
One wrong cell makes the entire output fail, so spatially plausible but imprecise predictions receive no partial credit.
Incorrect border-token predictions can crop to the wrong shape even when interior colors are otherwise correct.
Rules that are not invariant to scaling or translation can be blurred by the augmentation assumptions, while rotations and color permutations can alter semantics despite separate auxiliary tokens.
Underdetermined demonstrations can support multiple rules not covered by only two returned modes.
Larger ViTs can fit training data better while generalizing worse, as the 66M result shows.
ARC-2 distribution shift sharply reduces accuracy, suggesting the learned priors do not transfer to many harder tasks.
Task-token adaptation may settle into different local optima across runs; the ensemble exploits repeated runs but does not quantify this instability.
Attention maps can look structured on an incorrect task and should not be used as a correctness diagnostic.
reusable_insights: For categorical 2D problems, expanding a tiny symbol vocabulary into local patch configurations can supply useful inductive bias without natural-image pretraining.
Test-time learning and test-time augmentation solve different problems: adaptation fits a task rule, while multiple views expose candidate diversity and voting selects among it.
Always report single-view, multi-view, and pass@k separately; otherwise candidate-generation gains can be mistaken for stronger single-solution reasoning.
A pass@large-k gap is a direct diagnostic of ranking failure and motivates learned or constraint-based candidate selection.
Explicit background and boundary tokens can unify variable-size structured outputs, but their own error rates and ablations should be measured.
Task diversity can matter more than additional examples after a point, as the RE-ARC and task-count curves jointly suggest.
Independent adaptation can protect pretrained knowledge when joint test-batch optimization causes interference.
Small, heterogeneous architecture ensembles can add coverage when their inductive biases and errors differ.
open_questions: Does VARC retain its ARC-1 advantage under matched synthetic data, update counts, candidate budgets, and H100-hours against HRM, TRM, and latent-program methods?
How much of the 27.7-point ablation gain belongs independently to 2D coordinates, patch cardinality, canvas size, translation, scale, masking, and shape tokens?
Can a learned verifier or consistency constraint close the gap from 54.5 pass@2 toward 66.3 pass@300 without oracle access?
Which ARC task families fail on ARC-2, and do failures arise from representation, adaptation, proposal generation, shape decoding, or voting?
How sensitive are results to RE-ARC generator quality, generator authorship, number of variants, and held-out transformation families?
Can parameter-efficient or closed-form task adaptation replace 100 full test-time epochs while retaining accuracy?
Do attention heads or task-token neighborhoods causally encode reusable visual operations under intervention, not just correlate with human descriptions?
Would explicitly representing objects, relations, or executable transformations improve the simple-human-task failures without sacrificing the vision prior?
What calibration or abstention strategy is appropriate when demonstrations are genuinely ambiguous?
How does accuracy scale with views, adaptation seeds, wall time, and energy, and where do returns saturate?

competitive_landscape.title: Tackling the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus with Vision Transformers: the Importance of 2D Representation, Positions, and Objects
competitive_landscape.difference: ViTARC v2 adds pixel-level, spatial, and object-aware representations and fits task-specific models with abundant generated examples, but does not solve unseen tasks under ARC's few-shot cross-task protocol. VARC's narrower but meaningful advance is to combine a canvas-based vision representation with shared offline training and per-unseen-task adaptation; this predecessor prevents claiming that ARC had not previously been studied with ViTs.

competitive_landscape.title: Hierarchical Reasoning Model
competitive_landscape.difference: HRM v3 uses coupled recurrent modules operating at different timescales and reports 40.3/5.0 on ARC-1/ARC-2 in VARC's table. VARC instead adapts a visual encoder and votes over augmented views, reporting 54.5/8.3, but the papers do not share a matched data, update, or inference-compute protocol.

competitive_landscape.title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: TRM v1 simplifies recurrent reasoning to a two-layer 7M-parameter network and reports 44.6/7.8 in VARC's ARC-1/ARC-2 table. The 18M VARC reaches 54.5/8.3 through visual priors, synthetic offline data, 100-epoch adaptation, and 510-view voting; the ARC-2 separation is only 0.5 points and no matched replication is given.

competitive_landscape.title: Searching Latent Program Spaces
competitive_landscape.difference: LPN v3 learns a latent space of implicit programs and optimizes a compact latent code at test time, bridging program search and neural prediction. VARC instead updates a vision model/task token from pixel pairs and has no explicit latent-program variable; comparing the two would distinguish visual representation gains from the choice of adaptation space.

competitive_landscape.title: Combining Induction and Transduction for Abstract Reasoning
competitive_landscape.difference: This v4 system trains both a program-induction model and a direct transduction model on synthetic variants of Python solutions, finding complementary strengths and ensembling them. VARC is purely transductive at the output level and encodes spatial rather than executable-program bias, so its novelty is not the first trainable cross-task ARC learner but a vision-native alternative.

competitive_landscape.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Test-Time Training for Few-Shot Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: This v2 work fine-tunes an 8B language model on ARC demonstrations and reports 53.0 percent public-validation accuracy, or 61.9 percent when ensembled with program synthesis. VARC reuses the same broad parameter-update principle with an 18M vision model trained from scratch on ARC-derived data, then adds scale/translation views; the mechanism of test-time learning itself is prior work.

competitive_landscape.title: Product of Experts with LLMs: Boosting Performance on ARC Is a Matter of Perspective
competitive_landscape.difference: The v2 Product-of-Experts system uses task augmentations, depth-first candidate search, and an LLM as both generator and scorer, reporting 71.6 percent on the public ARC-AGI evaluation set. VARC is much smaller and avoids language pretraining but reports 60.4 with an eight-adaptation ensemble; the competitor shows that augmentation plus explicit candidate scoring can outperform majority voting at different resource assumptions.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors present ARC as an overlooked vision problem, claim a vision-native image-to-image framework trained from scratch on ARC data, and report that an 18M ViT substantially beats from-scratch recurrent systems while an ensemble matches average ARC-1 human performance.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Pages 1-2 frame the vision-centric claim; pages 3-5 specify the canvas, ViT, task token, adaptation, and voting; pages 6-7 report the ablations and system scores; pages 11-12 disclose the training scale and appendix results.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The durable novelty is narrower: VARC is the first demonstrated cross-task ARC solver in this reviewed panel to combine a categorical image canvas, conventional ViT/U-Net backbones, 2D scale/translation priors, per-task gradient adaptation, and exact-grid multi-view voting at this performance. Vision Transformers for ARC, test-time training, synthetic ARC expansion, and cross-task neural ARC solvers all predate it. The 60.4 headline further depends on RE-ARC generators, 100 adaptation epochs, 510 views, eight adapted ensemble components, and ARC-1; ARC-2 at 11.1 sharply limits the broad claim that ARC as a whole is primarily solved by the vision formulation.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text review of the exact 17-page cached arXiv PDF, SHA-256 0f7c95b5243039fb95827b1f440fd548a96431fb79db551dadf9ebb53e9cb1e0, whose official arXiv record was still v1 on 2026-08-23. Every extracted page had usable text; all tables, plotted values, captions, failure examples, attention maps, and appendix pages were also inspected in the rendered PDF. Competitor records were checked on official current arXiv pages/API on 2026-08-23 and pinned to the listed revisions. Attribution marks author reports separately from reviewer inference and contradiction/confound audits. This is a primary review, not an independent second passage check, so the depth remains full_text rather than verified. The strongest unresolved validity risks are unmatched system budgets, synthetic-generator dependence, missing uncertainty for most cells, public-set reuse, and the large ARC-1-to-ARC-2 drop.
